candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Genesis
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Genesis, Section L.20. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13, ed. J. Gwynn / Schaff (1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Genesis (c. 360 AD)

'But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive'. Ephrem treats this verse as the providence-formula par excellence — the complete two-tier reading of history. Tewahedo providential-theology cites Gen 50:20 in close conjunction with Rom 8:28 ('all things work together for good to them that love God') as the OT-NT providence-pair. The verse is foundational in Tewahedo consolation literature: every personal harm submits to the larger divine purpose without thereby being justified or made non-harmful.
